text: Tychon AI demonstrates that the primary failure mode of classical PID-based frequency lock loops — heading-dependent line-pulling from overlapping NV hyperfine structure — is correctable by a bounded INT8 FCNN operating as an asymmetry de-embedder on a radiation-tolerant FPGA.

At mission-relevant timescales, the AI-augmented loop reduces Allan deviation at the half-orbit period (τ = 2,700 s) by 96.1% (25.9× deviation reduction), from 16.66 µT to 0.64 µT — demonstrating that the CNN flattens the long-duration drift curve that renders classical PID unusable for orbital navigation.

The complete hybrid control loop — SmartHLS PID (II=1, ~48 ns latency, 3,000× margin over the 150 µs budget) plus VectorBlox-accelerated INT8 CNN (12.5 KB `.vnnx`) — synthesizes on the MPFS250T PolarFire SoC at 25.90% LUT utilization.

All five constrained clock domains pass post-place-and-route timing closure under multi-corner static timing analysis (slow_lv_lt, fast_hv_lt, slow_lv_ht); the worst-case design slack is **+0.728 ns on the 125 MHz PLL OUT0 domain**, with the critical path internal to the integrated PID compute datapath, and the VectorBlox PLL at 100/200 MHz passes within V1000 design margins.[^slack-ref] Total subsystem power is ~5.2 W (FPGA fabric + MSS) per SmartPower post-P&R analysis.

The system is bounded by a hardware-enforced Simplex RTA safety architecture that guarantees absolute stability via the Circle Criterion under sector saturation clamps (Decision-2-Option-C hardcoded outer + AXI-tightenable inner) and slew-rate limiting; an inference-deadline watchdog with bumpless transfer is fully synthesized and instantiated in fabric, with the watchdog timer driving `ai_watchdog_timeout` from a 200,000-cycle counter at 200 MHz.

Note: the April 2 baseline (`r1_s1`, +2.107 ns on PLL OUT0) is from a superseded paper-shell closure on a SmartDesign top in which `nv_pid_top_0` had been pruned by Synplify CL168 and constant-folded; r6_s25 is the authoritative integrated-PID-in-loop closure for Phase I.
Worst-case design slack +0.728 ns on PLL OUT0 (125 MHz, internal to the PID arithmetic datapath, source: `MPFS_ICICLE_KIT_BASE_DESIGN_timing_r6_s25.rpt`).

Three hardware-enforced boundaries in the FPGA fabric guarantee BIBO stability: sector saturation clamps (±4.5% actuator range, ±2.25 µT for a 50 µT operating field), slew-rate limiting on the AI output derivative, and an inference-deadline watchdog (200,000-cycle counter at 200 MHz, 1.0 ms timeout) that drives deterministic bumpless transfer (rising-edge detector, integral state back-calculation `I_new = I_old + u_AI_old`, 5.0 µs cooldown).

Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) diamond magnetometers offer a promising pathway for GPS-independent navigation, with demonstrated room-temperature sensitivities reaching 18 pT/√Hz [Stürner et al., 2021] and 9.4 pT/√Hz without cryogenic assistance [Clevenson et al., 2015].

A µs-class classical PID loop stabilizes the NV ensemble at high bandwidth (<150 µs), while an INT8-quantized CNN (accelerated by VectorBlox on the RT PolarFire SoC) provides <1 ms adaptive bias cancellation for heading-dependent and thermally-induced errors that the PID cannot resolve.
The bounded hybrid architecture ensures the AI can never destabilize the sensor — only improve it.
![Figure 1: Concept of operations — AI-cognitive engine for quantum PNT, with the three-boundary safety triad (clamp + slew + watchdog) on the RT PolarFire SoC.](media/image1.png)

The foundational stabilization is governed by a strictly proper, deterministic classical PID controller (SmartHLS C++, ~48 ns latency at 125 MHz), ensuring mathematically verifiable, high-bandwidth linear tracking.

The outer stage is a hardcoded `OUTER_SECTOR_CLAMP_FRACTION = 0.045` (`hls/include/rta_config.hpp:19`), synthesized as an immediate constant and untouchable by AXI or SEU; for the nominal `out_max=5V`, `out_min=0V` actuator range this gives a ±0.225 V outer bound.

**Slew-Rate Limiting (Temporal Limit).** The discrete derivative `du_AI/dt` is clamped in hardware to `MAX_SLEW_PER_CYCLE = 0.001` (Q16.16, `hls/include/rta_config.hpp:24`); at 200 MHz fabric clock this corresponds to 200 V/ms maximum actuator command rate.
A third boundary — an inference-deadline watchdog that triggers deterministic bumpless transfer at the 1.0 ms timeout — is **fully instantiated** in the Phase I integrated overlay.

The watchdog driver is a standalone hand-coded Verilog module (`hdl/watchdog_timer.v`, 200 MHz × 200,000-cycle counter with `$clog2`-derived width) instantiated in the SmartDesign top as `watchdog_timer_0`.

The placed netlist confirms the instance survives synthesis: `watchdog_timer_0/Primitives` consumes 26 LUTs and 20 DFFs per `polarfire-hybrid-control/libero/reports/2026-04-29-pid-real/MPFS_ICICLE_KIT_BASE_DESIGN_compile_netlist_hier_resources.csv` (r6_s25 closure).

The trigger logic inside `nv_pid_top_0` (rising-edge detector on `ai_watchdog_timeout`, cooldown counter at `WATCHDOG_COOLDOWN_CYCLES = 1000` = 5.0 µs at 200 MHz) is also present in the placed netlist alongside the integrator, multipliers, clamps, and slew-limit registers.

At these field strengths, the directional Zeeman splitting (~1.4 MHz) falls below the ensemble linewidth (~2 MHz), collapsing the 8 NV resonance dips into one or two unresolved features.

This physics-driven insight led to the reformulation where the CNN acts as a bounded residual corrector for the PID's heading-dependent line-pulling error, achieving 54.3% reduction in scalar tracking error on held-out validation data and 96.1% reduction in Allan deviation at the half-orbit averaging time (25.9× deviation reduction at τ=2,700 s, direct OADEV).
By predicting a ±2.25 µT residual instead of absolute 0–100 µT, the INT8 quantization achieves ~19 nT/bit effective resolution — a 20× improvement in dynamic range utilization.

**Scope.** Phase I delivered a physics-based synthetic data generator for CW-ODMR spectra targeting NV-diamond magnetometers in the bulk-ensemble regime, suitable for training and validating the cognitive control engine described in Section 6.

Constructing the NV ensemble Hamiltonian `H = D·S_z² + γ_e·B·S + Σ A·S·I`, where D is the zero-field splitting (~2.87 GHz), γ_e is the electron gyromagnetic ratio, B is the (3D) external magnetic field vector, and A captures hyperfine coupling to the ¹⁴N (axial) and lattice ¹³C nuclei. 2.

Throughput: **~8 ms/spectrum on DGX Spark**; the **50,000-sample production dataset generates in ~4 minutes**. - **Validation path:** Full numerical Hamiltonian diagonalization via SimOS for cross-checking the analytical fast path.
This ensures the Lindblad master equation captures state-mixing and cross-couplings inherently, rather than layering them on after the fact.

- **Temperature `T(t)`:** OU process with mean 300 K, range 280–320 K, correlation time matched to expected on-orbit thermal cycling (Phase I uses representative bench-top values; Phase II will refine against SGP4-derived thermal trajectories under Priority 3, Section 9.4).
The linear ZFS temperature coefficient `dD/dT ≈ −74.2 kHz/K` (textbook NV-diamond value) is applied to D in the time-evolved Hamiltonian.

Validated against SBQuantum's thermal cycling data: −65 °C to +125 °C for 335+ hours, ~400 pT/√Hz vector sensitivity sustained, heading errors below 5 nT [arXiv:2509.19179, 2025]. - **Microwave drive amplitude `B₁(t)`:** Cascaded OU process **coupled** to `T(t)` via a thermal coefficient `α_B1 ≈ −0.35%/°C` — a representative coupling for solid-state MW power amplifiers and impedance-matched drive networks.

The coupling is the v4 critical change relative to v3: in v3, T and B₁ were independent post-processing terms; in v4, B₁ inherits its slow drift from T directly. - **P1 spin-bath decoherence:** Lorentzian power spectral density `S(ω) = Δ²·2τ_c / (1 + ω²τ_c²)` with `Δ ~ 1–7 MHz` and `τ_c ~ 5–50 µs`, parameter ranges drawn from the CCE study [arXiv:2503.05404] and the OU-process treatment in arXiv:2312.12643.
Quantitative justification: a 1.5% asymmetric shift on a 2 MHz linewidth produces a ~30 kHz tracking offset, equivalent to ~1,000 nT of systematic measurement error.
- Allan deviation curves from the synthetic generator match the SBQuantum NV magnetometer profile: white-noise scaling (`τ⁻¹/²`) up to ~5 s averaging time, then thermal-drift dominance.

The pre-AIC test split therefore shares the train-split corruption distribution by construction — a worst-case for inverse-crime contamination. - A re-evaluation was performed on `production_50k_v2_aic`, regenerated under active AIC shifts. v1 (trained on the pre-AIC dataset) achieves **54.21% test MAE reduction on the AIC-shifted test set**, versus **54.07% on the pre-AIC test split** — a difference of **+0.14 percentage points**. - v1 generalizes cleanly across the AIC distribution gap.
This is consistent with the Phase II generalization expectation for the FCNN architecture (Section 8.3).
